scope: Pinned-author-version method reproduction and all declared core simulation comparisons, including two verified execution corrections; not a certified original 2024 release.

primary_table1.reference_groups: acados and naive retain their original foothold-restored trajectory paths; the corrected adaptive pair consists of 100 new episodes.

supported_findings: All original three base methods complete 60 s Figure 3 tracking in the fixed +/-5 N/Nm reconstruction.
Corrected adaptive frequency increases under the 40 N push and returns to nominal; both compared controllers survive the declared 8 s reconstruction.
The corrected same-implementation frequency contrast improves 60 s no-fall outcomes from 0/50 to 22/50 and mean time without a fall from 7.93536 to 42.72 s; 48/50 paired seeds last longer.

Clock correction reduces >3 cm continuing-swing reference jumps from 71.83 percent to 0.206 percent. Its +4.70 s paired mean lifetime change has a 95 percent interval spanning zero; a reliable lifetime improvement from that correction alone is not established.
remaining_gap: Original Figure 4 full velocity commands and unambiguous push timing remain unavailable; caption and main text disagree about push duration. The previously executed reconstruction does not reproduce the reported acados fall. Original Table I episode duration, initialization/phase, full wrench generation/timing and failure definition remain unavailable in the selected paper and dated author source. The remaining difference cannot be uniquely assigned to protocol versus retained modern implementation choices.
required_external_evidence: Original Figure 4 full velocity command, push timing and controller/helper configuration.
Original Table I episode duration, reset/phase settings, wrench generation/timing, failure definition, and controller/model parameter snapshot.
real_robot_status: Original Aliengo experiments unperformed; later H stage.
latest_findings: Among the three tested fixed frequencies, 2.4 Hz has the highest observed 60 s completion (28/50) and capped mean duration (46.3486 s). Retain it as a strong fixed-frequency baseline in subsequent authorized comparisons.

Adaptive completes 22/50 and lasts 42.72 s on average. Adaptive-minus-fixed-2.4 paired duration is -3.6286 s, 95% interval [-10.250129,2.904257]; success difference is -12 percentage points, interval [-30,6]. Neither superiority nor equivalence between these two controllers is established.

On the 15 seeds where both adaptive and fixed 2.4 Hz complete 60 s, adaptive uses 1574.064 J less positive mechanical work on average (95% paired interval [-1927.053,-1158.756] J), while its velocity RMSE is 0.023942 m/s higher (interval [0.009092,0.042247]). This is a completion-conditioned mechanical-work comparison, not battery energy or an unconditional all-task efficiency claim.

All three new Fig. 3 methods complete 60 s. Steady MPC-interface calls stay below 10 ms, but complete online steps exceed 2 ms on 14.55%, 16.14%, and 16.33% of recorded steps (acados, naive, MPPI). This does not establish real-robot 500 Hz operation.
